events.details: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors. From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova , artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. events.title: Wetland Wednesdays: Phragmites Control and Native Planting at Van Cortlandt Park
events.description: Volunteer wetland restoration at Van Cortlandt Lake: cut invasive phragmites and plant native willows and shrubs. Wednesdays in October, 9 am - 12 pm.
events.details: Join the Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland restoration along Van Cortlandt Lake. We cut back invasive phragmites (common reed) that crowds out native wetland plants and, as plants arrive, plant native willows and shrubs at the restoration sites. Dates include Wednesdays weekly from October 7th - October 28th. Dates are 10/7, 10/14, 10/21, and 10/28. Meeting Details: Location: Van Cortlandt Golf House. Meet outside the VCPA offices next to the bathrooms. Time: 9:00 am - 12:00 pm. What to Bring: Long sleeves, long pants and boots (phragmites stems are sharp and the ground is wet) Water and a snack Tools, gloves and training provided; no experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Groups of 6 or more, please email noel@vancortlandt.org first.

events.title: Neighborhood Stories: Sharing New York Memories
events.description: Join us at the historic Hall of Records on October 21st to learn about the City\u0092s oral history initiative, Neighborhood Stories!
events.details: On Wednesday, October 21st, the NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) presents Reflecting on NYC History: A Community Forum, a full day of programming at the historic Hall of Records. Earlier this year, DORIS launched a new website for the Neighborhood Stories project, a unique storytelling initiative that gathers and permanently preserves oral history-style interviews with New York City residents, connecting local history with the records of City government maintained in the collections of the Municipal Archives and Library. Join us at 11:00 AM to learn how you can share your New York memories and help preserve the history of the city and its neighborhoods. Drawing on photographs, documents, maps, and other materials from the Archives, we\u0092ll explore how the official record and personal stories can tell different sides of the same place, community, or moment in New York\u0092s history. Bring\u0097or simply think of\u0097a photograph, object, memory, or family story connected to New York. Come ready to look closely, share a memory, ask questions, and consider what you or someone you know might contribute to the growing record of New York life. Learn how the project began, how to get involved, and how your story can help preserve New York City history for future generations.

events.description: Join us as researchers Hugh Ryan and Riah Lee Kinsey discuss their experiences navigating archival spaces while researching LGBTQ history.
events.details: On Wednesday, October 21st, the NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) presents Reflecting on NYC History: A Community Forum, a full day of programming at the historic Hall of Records. Join us at 1:00 PM for a conversation with author Hugh Ryan and archivist Riah Lee Kinsey. The speakers will discuss their experiences conducting archival research at a range of institutions, with a particular focus on their work at the Municipal Archives and Library. Discover how their research has shaped their understanding of present-day New York and informed the ways they interpret LGBTQ history. The conversation will be moderated by archivist Tara Hart. Join us either virtually (via Zoom) or in person (limited seats available).

events.title: AI and NYC Government Records: Perspectives from the Department of Records & Information Services
events.description: Join us for a cross-departmental conversation with DORIS staff on how AI is affecting municipal archive services.
events.details: On Wednesday, October 21st, the NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) presents Reflecting on NYC History: A Community Forum, a full day of programming at the historic Hall of Records. At 3:00 PM, join the NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) for a cross?departmental conversation on how artificial intelligence is reshaping records management, archival practice, digital preservation, and public research services. This moderated panel brings together staff from across DORIS to discuss: \u0095 The rise of AI?generated research requests and how they challenge existing workflows \u0095 AI\u0092s potential to support metadata creation, digitization, technical tasks, and preservation planning \u0095 Ethical concerns around accuracy, privacy, bias, and transparency \u0095 How AI may influence the definition, creation, and stewardship of government records \u0095 Opportunities and limitations for integrating AI into archival decision?making Moderator: Caleb Simone, Digital Archivist Panelists: Katie Ehrlich, Reference Supervisor Patricia Glowinski, Collections Management Supervisor Rossy Mendez, Reference Supervisor Kelli O\u0092Toole, Digital Programs Supervisor Rose Nagle?Yndigoyen, Director of NYC Records Management Lindsey Hobbs, Head of Conservation & Preservation As part of New York Archives Week, this program highlights DORIS\u0092s role in shaping the broader conversation about AI, archives, and city government, while bringing together diverse staff perspectives on the opportunities and challenges ahead.

events.details: On Wednesday, October 21st, the NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) presents Reflecting on NYC History: A Community Forum, a full day of programming at the historic Hall of Records. Join us at 6:00 PM for the opening of Change Preservation! Curated by architects Wes Hiatt and Violette de la Selle, the exhibition brings together the material of Changing Change, a research project shown in two chapters at Citygroup in 2024 and 2025 on how buildings in Manhattan's Lower East Side and Chinatown endure through constant alteration. Patterns of Change layers current conditions over 1940s tax photographs and permit application drawings held at the Municipal Archives, documenting blocks and buildings as they were and as they are. Keep the Change illustrates that history with articulated composite drawings that present each building's many lives at once. Presented at the NYC Department of Records & Information Services, where the source information is held, the drawings read as both evidence and argument. The drawings advocate that the centuries-old buildings of the Lower East Side stand as manifestos for a mode of preservation that contrasts with the one in effect: unconstrained by a particular historical appearance \u0097 pristine and immutable \u0097 they contribute meaningfully to their communities, taking on different aspects as they adapt to the changing circumstances that keep them in use. What if preservation frameworks could embrace and even facilitate degrees of change rather than requiring high-fidelity restorations? At 7:00 PM, immediately following the opening, there will be a live podcast interview with Shawn(ta) Smith-Cruz, the commissioner of the NYC Department of Records & Information Services (DORIS).

events.title: SeedMoney Grant Info Session
events.description: Learn how to raise real money for your garden through crowdfunding.
events.details: Learn how to raise real money for your garden through crowdfunding. The SeedMoney Challenge is a free, 30-day online fundraising campaign (November 15 to December 15) where food gardens raise funds from their own supporters and earn a share of 432 challenge grants of $100 to $1,000. There are no fees and no fundraising experience is needed. Last year, Rows for the Hungry, a New Jersey donation garden, raised $11,820 from 122 donors, plus $1,100 in grants. Join SeedMoney's founder to see how it works, then apply by November 12. Register Here NYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation's most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. events.title: Person Place Thing with Randy Cohen & DORIS Commissioner Shawn(ta) Smith-Cruz
events.description: Join Randy Cohen and DORIS Commissioner Shawn(ta) Smith-Cruz for a live recording of Person Place Thing at the NYC Surrogate\u0092s Courthouse!
events.details: On Wednesday, October 21st, the NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) presents Reflecting on NYC History: A Community Forum, a full day of programming at the historic Hall of Records. At 7:00 PM, the NYC Department of Records & Information Services (DORIS)\u0092 commissioner, Shawn(ta) Smith-Cruz, will join Emmy Award winner Randy Cohen for a live recording of Person Place Thing. Person Place Thing is an interview show based on the idea that people are especially engaging when they speak, not directly about themselves, but about something they care about. Guests share a person, place, and thing they find meaningful. The result: surprising stories from great talkers. Join us either virtually (via Zoom) or in person (limited seats available). Music will be provided by: Liz Hanley Note: If you are interested in attending this event in person, please select the \u0093In-Person Attendance\u0094 ticket option when RSVPing for this event.
